messages:
maya: Seeing 429s from a Dedicated tenant (org=acme-prod) even though they have reserved throughput 200 req/s. Happened during steady traffic. Request IDs: r-12a, r-12b.
jorge: Can you paste the 429 payload? Is it "per_key" vs "tenant_isolation"?
maya: payload: "error":"quota_exceeded","reason":"tenant_node_quota"; no spike in traffic.
tess: We changed per-node credit accounting recently (short TTL for node leases). Could be routing causing requests to land on a node that depleted its credits.
deniz: If routing flips between nodes frequently, node-local buckets can be exhausted despite pool-level capacity. Did routing logs show churn?
maya: Yes — requests for acme-prod were routed round-robin between pool-x and pool-y every ~25s due to probe-based rebalancing. pool-y had transient inflight high.
jorge: Two approaches: 1) make tenant credits backed by a pool-global counter (stronger correctness), 2) prefer sticky routing for reserved tenants, 3) surface node_hint in 429 response for debug. Trade-offs?
tess: Sticky routing for reserved tenants (TTL ~2m) seems lowest-risk and avoids cross-node coordination. Pool-global requires distributed counters + lease and risk of higher latency for credit check.
maya: We should also fix inflight accounting: KV-prefetch and internal sub-ops currently increment inflight separately which double-counts. That reduces effective concurrency for tenants.
deniz: Proposal: treat all child ops as part of parent request for inflight counts. Only increment at root enqueue, decrement at final completion. We'll need load tests.
jorge: I'll draft the inflight accounting PR (ENG-PLATFORM-3011). Will add unit tests + a K6 load scenario to replicate the double-counting.
tess: I'll draft a canary plan: enable sticky routing + new inflight accounting for 1% of reserved tenants for 48h. Metrics: tenant_429_rate, p95 latency, effective throughput. Rollback criteria if 429_rate increases or tail latency degrades >10%.
deniz: I'll add infra metrics: dedicated.tenant.node_credit_exhausted{tenant, node} and add routed_node in traces (header X-Redwood-Node) so we can pivot.
product-ops: For Console: show a "node saturation" band in reserved tenant timeline with hover: "Node-level throttle; routing attempt to other nodes may fail until node recovers." Also add a link to troubleshooting docs.
maya: Let's also include better 429 body so support teams can triage without cluster access: include fields: "reason":"tenant_node_quota","node_hint":"pool-y","retry_after_secs":2
jorge: Sounds good. Who owns what?
deniz: I'll own metrics + trace header (ENG-INFRA-1199) and wired dashboard panels for canary.
tess: I'll own canary runbook + risk matrix and console mock (ENG-CONSOLE-623).
jorge: I'll own the inflight accounting change + tests (ENG-PLATFORM-3011). Ping maya for review.
maya: OK. Canary start: 2025-10-09T10:00:00Z. Alert: if canary tenant_429_rate doesn't drop by >=50% in first 2h, auto pause and page SRE.
deniz: Adding temporary dashboard tile "node_hint 429s" for triage.
product-ops: Marking support docs update: add KB "Dedicated 429s: node_hint troubleshooting".
sre-bot: Canary ENG-PLATFORM-3011 scheduled for 2025-10-09T10:00:00Z by deniz.
